topic: What Actually Stops a Bot From Hammering Your API

claims.text: API Gateway throttles requests using the token bucket algorithm, where a token counts for a request.
In the token bucket algorithm, a burst can allow a pre-defined overrun of the rate limits.
When request submissions exceed the steady-state rate and burst limits, API Gateway begins to throttle, and clients may receive 429 Too Many Requests errors.
AWS applies throttles on a best-effort basis; they should be thought of as targets rather than guaranteed request ceilings.
Besides bursts, other factors can also cause throttle limits to be overrun in some cases.
Token-bucket rate limiting allows controlled bursts of traffic while maintaining a steady average request rate, unlike fixed-window limits.
In the token bucket model, the bucket refills at a constant rate over time.
API Gateway lets developers configure rate and burst throttling limits per route, overriding account-level defaults.
API Gateway applies account-level and method-level throttling limits.
